Glossary

What every term in the Wardrobe Diary means. These definitions are what the app computes and what AI assistants get through the MCP server; each links to the metric that computes it.

Semantic layer version 0.4.0 (2026-10-16) · JSON-LD · source (YAML) · CC BY 4.0

Garment

One physical piece of clothing, footwear or accessory in the wardrobe, owned at some point since tracking began.

Identical items bought together are separate garments, each with its own wears.

Related: Category, Ownership period

Category

A kind of clothing that groups garments. The 13 categories, in their standard order: Jackets and hoodies, Blazers and vests, Knits, Shirts, T-shirts and tanks, Pants, Shorts, Belts, Socks, Shoes, Underwear shirts, Underwear boxers, Sportswear.

Categories are always listed in this order, never alphabetically.

Start of tracking

1 January 2018, the first day of the daily log.

Garments bought earlier count as owned from this date; their earlier wears are pre-tracking wears.

Wear also: use

One garment worn on one day, as logged. Wearing a garment more than once on the same day is still one wear.

Wears logged outside the garment's ownership period are ignored by every metric.

Pre-tracking wears also: times used init

The number of times a garment was worn before tracking began, entered once as an estimate.

They count only in figures whose range starts on the start of tracking, and always in lifetime wears.

Price

What was paid for the garment, in euros, rounded to whole cents.

Second-hand garments have the price actually paid. Multipacks are split evenly per item.

Ownership period

The days a garment counts as owned: from its purchase date, but no earlier than the start of tracking, to its divest date, both inclusive.

Related: Active, Divested

Active

A garment is active on a day if that day is within its ownership period.

The divest day itself still counts as owned (as in the original R pipeline).

Divested

No longer owned after the divest date, because it was sold, given away, recycled or discarded.

Date range

The period a figure is computed for, from a start date to an end date, both inclusive. Every metric takes a date range; the default is from the start of tracking to the last logged day.

Decision: 2026-10-08-ranges

As of

A figure computed as it was known on a past date, counting only wears logged up to then. Used by the animated charts.

The one deliberate exception to the lifetime rule of cost per wear (decision D-2).

Times worn

The number of wears of a garment within the date range, plus its pre-tracking wears when the range starts on the start of tracking.

Computed by: Times worn

Lifetime wears

All wears of a garment over its whole ownership period, including pre-tracking wears.

Computed by: Lifetime wears

Cost per wear also: CPW, cost per use

For a garment: its price divided by its lifetime wears, regardless of the date range chosen. A garment never worn costs its full price. For a category: the sum of the prices of its garments owned in the range divided by the sum of their lifetime wears, so unworn garments count with their full price (divided by 1 if none has ever been worn).

Using lifetime wears, even wears after the range ends, keeps the concept consistent: a garment has one cost per wear, which falls as it gets more use, and a category's cost per wear is what its garments cost over all the use they get. The date range decides only which garments count.

Computed by: Cost per wear (garment) · Decision: D-2

Use-weighted average

An average in which each garment counts as many times as it was worn in the range.

Wears per month

Times worn divided by the months owned in the range, where a month is 30.5 days.

Computed by: Wears per month

Days used also: frequency of use, category frequency of use

For a category: the share of days on which at least one of its garments was worn, counted from the later of the range start and the day the category's first garment was owned, to the range end.

Computed by: Days used

Yearly cost

What a year of using a category costs at the current rate - its cost per wear × 365 × days used.

Computed by: Yearly cost

Monthly cost

Yearly cost divided by 12. Used to compare clothing categories with other monthly spending.

Computed by: Monthly cost

Inventory value

The sum of the prices of the garments active on the range's end date.

Computed by: Inventory value

Active items also: items

The number of garments active on the range's end date.

Computed by: Active items

Inventory turnover also: turnover

Yearly cost divided by inventory value - the share of the wardrobe's purchase value "used up" per year.

Computed by: Inventory turnover

Second hand share

The share of the garments active on the range's end date that were bought second hand (a count, not a value share).

Computed by: Second hand share

Daily cost

For a day, the sum of the cost per wear of the garments worn that day (and owned then).

The Dashboard leaves Sportswear out of its daily cost charts.

Computed by: Daily cost · Decision: Q-1

Worn together also: combination, outfit companion

Two garments are worn together on a day when both are logged as worn that day.

Computed by: Worn together

Final (daily cost) also: all divested

A day's cost is final when every garment worn that day has been divested, so it can no longer fall.

Tag

A descriptive label from a fixed vocabulary. Tags only describe garments; they never change any calculation.

Second hand (tag)

Bought second hand, i.e. used before. The price is what was paid and wears count from the purchase, without estimating earlier use.

Related: Tag

Hanko (tag)

Kept at the summer home in Hanko, so worn only during stays there.

Related: Tag

Bicycle gear (tag)

Cycling gear.

Related: Tag

Motorcycle gear (tag)

Motorcycle gear.

Related: Tag

Winter / Summer (tags)

Worn mainly in winter or in summer; used to narrow the logging list by season.

Related: Tag

Materials

The garment's materials label as written, in free text (e.g. "Shell 100% polyamide, lining 100% polyester").

The text is never changed; it is interpreted on read into a material composition.

Main part

For a garment whose label lists several parts (shell, lining, padding…), the part that counts in material figures: the one whose label begins with shell, main, outer, body, fabric or belt, otherwise the first one listed.

Fibre

A material a garment is made of, under one normalised name (e.g. lycra and spandex are both elastane, nylon is polyamide).

Fibre class

Natural (cotton, wool, linen, leather, down, feather), regenerated cellulose (viscose, modal, lyocell), synthetic (polyester, polyamide, elastane, acrylic…) or other.

Estimated composition

A composition whose shares are not given on the label (or don't add up to 100 %), so the fibres are split equally or normalised.

Fibre mass

Weight × composition, summed per fibre. Owned basis: garments active on the range's end date. Worn basis: every wear in the range counts the garment's full weight.

Computed by: Fibre mass

Average outfit weight

The average total weight of the garments worn per logged day (garments with a known weight).

Computed by: Average outfit weight

Coverage

How much of the data a material figure could use - garments or wears with both a weight and readable materials, out of all.

Comparison item

An item of other everyday spending, such as a transport ticket or a streaming service, with a monthly cost and a use frequency.

Use frequency

For a comparison item, the share of days on which it is used (entered by the owner).

Cost per use (comparison)

For a comparison item, its monthly cost divided by (30.5 × use frequency).

Computed by: Cost per use (comparison item)
